units.function: Unit tests for systemd/launchd definition generation, lifecycle dispatch, drift repair, foreground-writer exclusion and unsafe-definition rejection.
units.dependencyDirection: Uses temporary home directories and injected command runners against the real service-manager classes; no real supervisor is mutated.
units.keyDataModels: Service definition, instance/service name, supervisor status, saved login enablement and command calls.
units.lifecycle: Render, install/repair, start/stop/uninstall, detect platform and guard a second foreground writer.
units.testAssessment: Focused Vitest passed 19/19. Strong escaping, drift and symlink/hardlink tests are present, but file modes/parent links, executable provenance, concurrency, timeouts, postconditions and rollback remain untested.
units.designRationale: Provide deterministic cross-platform user-service behavior without requiring privileged system services.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs safe, independently deployable local control/execution-node services with version/config provenance and recoverable lifecycle operations.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the injected runner, definition renderer and unsafe-file tests; add signed executable/config binding, hardened definitions, cross-process serialization, structured phase results and failure reconciliation.
units.responsibilityConflict: The tests have no operator identity, approved service/config digest or evidence that persistent authority was granted by an accountable human.

units.function: Tests for service doctor behavior, hot-restart lock serialization/stale recovery and local health URL handling.
units.dependencyDirection: Uses injected service/health fixtures plus real temporary restart-lock files.
units.keyDataModels: Service status, health/version response, instance restart lock and expected restart version.
units.lifecycle: Skip managed self-check, serialize restart callbacks, reclaim a dead-PID lock and classify healthy/conflicting runtime states.
units.testAssessment: Focused Vitest passed 7/7. PID reuse, cross-process races, lock filesystem trust, supervisor-to-health binding, drift errors and cleanup are absent.
units.designRationale: Prevent concurrent hot restarts and surface a foreground process conflicting with an installed service.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs trustworthy local-node diagnostics and restart coordination that preserve active work and responsibility evidence.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the explicit restart serialization and conflict projection, replacing PID-only locks with owner/start-time or OS locking and binding health/attestation to the exact runtime process and artifact.
units.responsibilityConflict: Successful health/restart tests do not prove who authorized the restart or whether active Agent work was drained/adopted without losing responsibility continuity.

units.function: Cross-platform user-service adapter for rendering and managing systemd user units or launchd agents.
units.dependencyDirection: Instance/home/shim paths become persistent supervisor definitions; OS commands and filesystem mutations implement lifecycle operations.
units.keyDataModels: ServiceManager/Status/InstallOptions, systemd unit, launchd plist, instance-scoped service names and log paths.
units.lifecycle: Detect supervisor, safely write/repair definition, enable/disable, start/stop/restart, inspect status, stream logs and optionally enable linger.
units.testAssessment: The focused suite passes, but important production failure and supply-chain boundaries are not exercised.
units.designRationale: Abstract platform differences behind one small local service interface and make definitions reproducible.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS self-hosted/local enterprise profiles need a portable service boundary for control plane and local Connector execution nodes.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT, not copy unchanged. Preserve the narrow adapter, but validate instance/path inputs, bind shim to signed managed-install provenance, harden OS definitions, use timeouts and return reconciled partial-state outcomes with rollback guidance.
units.responsibilityConflict: Persistent execution authority is installed without an operator/approval/artifact record, and the generic user service has the user's full ambient filesystem/network authority.

units.function: CLI surface for service lifecycle plus file-mediated hot restart, drain intent, health/version waiting and status/log output.
units.dependencyDirection: Commander options drive ServiceManager mutations; local config selects a health URL; instance files coordinate restart with the server.
units.keyDataModels: Service status, HealthResult, hot-restart lock token, intent/report document and expected version.
units.lifecycle: Resolve manager, mutate or inspect service; restart under a lock, write intent, restart supervisor, wait for health and optionally receive a drain/adoption report.
units.testAssessment: Only restart helper behavior is covered by the reviewed focused tests; command exit semantics, JSON purity, intent/report link safety, postconditions and rollback are not.
units.designRationale: Offer operationally useful lifecycle commands and preserve active Agent runs during binary/service restart.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must upgrade local execution nodes without losing work, evidence or responsibility continuity and must expose automatable stable outcomes.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE_ONLY for the current command implementation; ADAPT the restart protocol concept into a versioned, authenticated, atomic state machine with stable codes, process attestation, mandatory drain/adoption proof and rollback.
units.responsibilityConflict: Restart intent contains a run ID but no accountable human/approval or artifact/config digest. A missing preservation report remains a successful nullable result, so the claimed responsibility continuity is not proven.

units.function: Doctor checks for optional supervisor installation, exact definition drift, active runtime, local health/version and systemd linger.
units.dependencyDirection: Reads service definition and managed-install manifest, calls ServiceManager status and probes the configured local HTTP endpoint.
units.keyDataModels: CheckResult, ServiceStatus, rendered definition, managed version and local health response.
units.lifecycle: Skip unsupported/uninstalled states; compare definition; classify supervisor/runtime/health/version/linger and emit repair prose.
units.testAssessment: Focused health tests pass, but file provenance, manifest corruption, supervisor PID binding, spoofed responses and stable codes are not covered.
units.designRationale: Give self-hosted operators actionable diagnostics without requiring a background service.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs trustworthy, localizable diagnostics for cloud/local services and Connector nodes.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the layered checks, adding stable diagnostic codes/parameters, link/owner/mode and signed manifest checks, supervisor-runtime attestation and explicit degraded/unsupported states.
units.responsibilityConflict: Operational health is not responsibility evidence; the check cannot identify which approved runtime is serving or who owns remediation.
